messages.subject: Linear combinations after inla() call
parts:
Hi,

I wonder if it is possible to call INLA, say,

fit <- inla(...)

and then later infer some linear combinations from the "fit" object?

Thank you!

Regards, Gregor Gorjanc

messages.subject: Re: Linear combinations after inla() call
parts:
Yes, it makes sense only for derived linear combinations. Would be
nice to have possibility to run them after the model has been run
already, especially if you have large data and model, which takes a
long time to compute. This would also provide a way to use results
from a particular run for some fancy computations, which one might
think only after the model has been run. Just an idea.

gg

what you can do is to restart with previous result and then add the
lincomb, like

result = inla(...)

new.result = inla(..., lincomb=..., control.mode=list(result =result,
restart=FALSE))

meaning that it picks the mode from the 'result' and then start
integrating including computing the lincomb's. see ?control.mode
